inputs.text: This is a power grab dressed up as protection. The case against the abbot of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame gives officials a convenient example to make France’s “psychological subjection” law seem necessary, while its vagueness leaves room to target whatever beliefs become inconvenient. The community is being put on display to normalize a broader tool of control. The real warning isn’t about one abbot; it’s about who gets to define danger—and who benefits when dissent can be rebranded as harm.
